newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover surge in week to June 27.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover surge in week to June 27.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) saw its total turnover during the week ending June 27 doubling but traders insisted there were no major market movements causing the BSE turnover to surge 102.51 percent.
Total turnover rose to 82.107 million dinars in 139 transactions from 40.412 million dinars in 151 deals a week ago, the bourse said.
Traders said there were no dramatic changes on the market which caused such turnover rise, except for slightly lower interest rates and longer maturity of financial instruments trading on the market.

Higher turnover resulted from a sale of state T-bills worth 34.6 million dinars and due to a 25 million dinar turnover on the secondary market, with the National Bank of Yugoslavia selling bonds from its portfolio issued by the Serbian commodity Reserve Agency, traders said.
"State T-bills are close to their maturity and that is why the entire second tranche maturing July 11 has been sold out," a trader said.
Yugoslavia's government on May 12 put on sale for the first time 100 million dinars worth of 30-day and 60-day T-bills, which carry a nominal 4.5 percent monthly interest rate, to fill up the budget.
For the week ending June 27, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 115 transactions worth 18.997 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded eight times for a volume of 0.82 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between 6.00 and 13.00 percent per month, while maturity stood between seven and 360 days.
Traders saw high interest rates still the main factor preventing firms to deal on the bourse.

"Despite general shortage of cash, some funds are available. Although halved compared to the beginning of the year, interest rates of six to nine percent a month are still high and limit the interest," a trader said.
* There were three transactions in the central bank short-term bonds worth 1.9 million dinars.
* State T-bills were sold at the value of 34.6 million dinars in four transactions.
* Certificates of deposit traded five times for a volume of 0.32 million dinars.
* There were two transactions of wheat forward contracts worth 0.17 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 41.097 million dinars from 30.356 million the previous week.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, fell to 23.645 million dinars from 25.75 million. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
